column3: The Hebrew repeats anointing and consecrating at the end after first naming the objects; BSB states these actions once.
The Hebrew calls the leaders “heads of the house of their fathers”; BSB says “heads of their families.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has both “said” and “saying”; BSB gives a single “said.”
The Hebrew says “take” without explicitly naming “gifts” and repeats the service root; BSB says “Accept these gifts” and describes their use in the work.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls them “the sons of Gershon”; BSB uses “the Gershonites.”
The Hebrew calls them “the sons of Merari” and uses “by the hand of Ithamar”; BSB says “the Merarites” and “under the direction of Ithamar.”
The Hebrew uses singular “the shoulder” and calls the group “the sons of Kohath”; BSB uses plural “their shoulders” and “the Kohathites.”
The Hebrew names “the leaders” twice and uses singular “their offering”; BSB names them once and uses plural “their offerings.”
The Hebrew repeats “one leader for the day” twice, followed by plural “they shall present their offering”; BSB condenses this to one leader presenting his offering each day.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives the platter’s weight as “one hundred and thirty,” without explicitly repeating “shekels” for that first weight; BSB supplies the unit.
The Hebrew gives “ten gold” without an explicit weighing verb or the word “shekels”; BSB says “weighing ten shekels.”
The Hebrew calls the bull “a son of the herd” and the lamb “a son of its year”; BSB gives “young bull” and “a year old.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the lambs “sons of a year”; BSB says “a year old.”
The Hebrew says Nethanel “presented” an offering; BSB says he “drew near.”
